title: Underlying inflation pressure
data_fetch: Research Manager tidy delivery, fetched 12 Nov 2026, 17:24 Europe/Zurich. No new download by this script.

window.why: Pre-2020 sample (January 2000–December 2019) so the 2021–22 inflation spike does not inflate the standard deviation and flatten current z-scores. 2000–2019 is the longest stretch of the inflation-targeting era that is common to most of the series. Series that start after January 2000 use their available pre-2020 history, which is flagged.

method: Each series is signed so that a higher value means more inflation pressure, optionally smoothed with a 3-month average when the monthly series is noisy, then z-scored against the 2000–2019 mean and sample standard deviation (ddof=1). Z-scores are capped at ±3 before averaging. The aggregate is the equal-weight mean of components whose period-end is not more than three months before the as-of date. Latest available observation is used for daily, quarterly, survey and already-smooth monthly series. Core CPI 3-month annualised is also 3-month averaged because that series is noisy. The dial maps the aggregate onto [−3, +3], leaving room past the +1.5 ‘severe’ threshold; zone thresholds and labels are unchanged (green < −0.5, yellow −0.5..+0.5, orange +0.5..+1.5, red > +1.5). All z-scores and the aggregate are staff constructions (d).
method_note: Equal-weight mean of z-scores versus 2000–2019 (pre-2020, so 2021–22 does not flatten the scale). Noisy monthly series: 3-month average. Each z is capped at ±3; the dial maps −3 to +3. Public sources; Richmond is a staff construction (d). Shown without endorsement. A real-time (expanding-window) reading, using only data available at each date, is shown next to the headline score.
stale_rule: A component is stale, and is excluded from the aggregate, if the end of its reference period is more than three calendar months before the stale-check date (2026-11-13). It is still shown, flagged.

caveats: All z-scores and the aggregate are staff constructions (d), not official Reserve Bank or BLS indices.

The 2000–2019 window is a low and relatively stable inflation period. Readings around 3% therefore produce large positive z-scores, especially for core PCE (window sd is tight). That is the intended effect of excluding 2021–22 from the scaling window; it is not a statement about distance to the staff 3.2% core PCE baseline.

Atlanta Fed BIE only begins in October 2011, so its window is 2011–2019. That sample is very quiet (sd well below 0.2 percentage points) and enlarges the current z-score. The short window is flagged on the component.

GSCPI is published in standard-deviation units on the New York Fed's own historical scale (which includes 2020–22 and is revised in full every month). The gauge re-z-scores the published index against 2000–2019 and is therefore a different scale. The official NY Fed page has carried a “limited data” notice; the series is used as published, with the same credit and “shown without endorsement” line as the leading-indicator chart.

Richmond prices received on this gauge is the staff equal-weight mean of manufacturing and non-manufacturing “prices received, current”, the same staff construction (d) as on the public leading-indicator chart. It is not the official Richmond price measure.
Cleveland Fed EXPINF1YR is a model-based expectation (noncommercial use, DOI https://doi.org/10.26509/frbc-infexp), shown without endorsement.
5-year breakevens are inflation compensation, not pure expected inflation: they embed an inflation risk premium and TIPS liquidity effects.
Core PCE in the tidy file runs through September 2026 (October PCE had not been released at the 12 Nov tidy delivery). Core CPI 3-month annualised runs through October 2026.

Four official core year-over-year measures were added after Thomas cleared them for the public page with credit lines (13 Nov 2026, 07:11 Europe/Zurich): Cleveland Fed median CPI, Cleveland Fed 16% trimmed-mean CPI, Dallas Fed trimmed-mean PCE and Atlanta Fed sticky-price core CPI. The gauge uses only the 12-month (year-over-year) series from Research Manager's tidy files. Monthly annualized (m/m) values in the same files are not in the gauge and are not on the component charts.

Cleveland year-over-year values are the FRED vintage (MEDCPIM159SFRBCLE, TRMMEANCPIM159SFRBCLE), because the official Cleveland file has no 12-month column. Credit on each y/y row: “Source: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, via FRED”. Licensed CC BY-SA 4.0; derived charts are shared under the same licence. Cleveland documents October 2025 as interpolated (missing CPI month); values are used as published, not replaced.

Dallas Fed trimmed-mean PCE is one month behind (latest is Sep 2026; next update 25 Nov), following the PCE calendar. Credit: “Source: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas”. Dallas Fed terms permit reproduction with credit, provided it is not distributed for the purpose of private gain.
Atlanta Fed sticky-price core CPI (ex food and energy), year-over-year. Credit: “Source: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta”.

Equal weights treat a supply-chain index, a survey, a market breakeven, wages, import prices and realized core inflation as interchangeable. That is a transparent starting point, not an estimated factor model. Realized core (six of thirteen components: core PCE, core CPI, median CPI, trimmed-mean CPI, Dallas trimmed-mean PCE, sticky CPI) and leading/survey measures are mixed by design.
Licensed bank, broker, private-survey and survey-consensus figures are omitted from this gauge.

The headline aggregate is z-scored against 2000–2019, a window known only in hindsight. The real-time (expanding-window) reading as of 12 Nov 2026 is +0.31 (neutral): each component is z-scored only against its own history available before that date. A staff backtest found that neither reading is a reliable lead on Fed hikes or cuts.

aggregate_expanding.label: neutral
aggregate_expanding.window: expanding; at each date, each component is z-scored against its own history strictly before that date
aggregate_expanding.method: Same components, signs, smoothing, stale rule (period-end not more than three months before as-of) and ±3 cap as the headline aggregate. Equal-weight mean of components with a valid expanding z (13 of 13 as of 12 Nov 2026). Three-state label: low if z < −0.5, neutral if −0.5 ≤ z ≤ +0.5, high if z > +0.5. Current-vintage reconstruction, not a real-time data vintage (publication lags and revisions are not unwound). Staff construction (d).
aggregate_expanding.source: Staff backtest of the inflation-pressure gauge, computed 13 Nov 2026, 18:52 Europe/Zurich.
